rows.text: | Congo SARL capital | National decree 2017-41 art 4 lets members set SARL capital freely in the articles; art 5 requires equal shares with nominal value at least XAF 5,000. The OHADA default XAF 1,000,000 expressly yields to national rules and is not Congo's required minimum under this decree. | [Decree2017-41 arts4–5](https://acpce.cg/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/congo-decret_2017-41_sarl.pdf); ledger F02 |

rows.text: | SARL subscription and deposit | OHADA 311-1 requires all shares subscribed, in-kind shares fully paid, cash shares at least half paid at subscription with remainder within 2 years of RCCM registration. Congo decree 6–7 requires immediate deposit in a society-in-formation account at a qualifying bank/credit/microfinance institution with receipt; founders or a notary record payment/deposit with the prescribed declarations. | [OHADA311-1;Decree2017-41 arts6–7](https://acpce.cg/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/ACTE-UNIFORME-REVISE-RELATIF-AU-DROIT-DES-SOCIETES-COMMERCIALES-ET-DU-GROUPEMENT-DINTERET-ECONOMIQUE.pdf); ledger F03 |

rows.text: | SA and SAS capital | Ordinary SA minimum is XAF 10,000,000; cash subscription at least one-quarter paid, remainder within 3 years after RCCM. A listed/public-offer SA requires XAF 100,000,000 under 824. SAS capital/nominal is set by articles and it cannot make a public offering. Do not apply SA minimum mechanically to SAS. | [OHADA387–389,824,853-4–5](https://acpce.cg/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/ACTE-UNIFORME-REVISE-RELATIF-AU-DROIT-DES-SOCIETES-COMMERCIALES-ET-DU-GROUPEMENT-DINTERET-ECONOMIQUE.pdf); ledger F04 |

rows.text: | Displayed creation fees | The ACPCE public portal displays XAF 300,000 for SARL/SARLU and XAF 500,000 for SA/SAS/SASU. These are displayed creation taxes/fees, not paid-in capital or a quote for professional work. Applicable exemptions, amendments and ancillary costs require confirmation before payment. | [ACPCE public portal, Taxe unique de Création](https://monentreprise.acpce.cg/); ledger F10 |

rows.text: Select the legal form using F01. Prepare articles and appointments; verify the actual capital subscription, valuation and deposit rules for that form. Assemble F06–F08 documents and separate creation fees from capital. The national SARL rule supersedes the old default-minimum assertion. Plan accounting/audit under F13/F14 and the linked tax Guides.

rows.text: | Entity choice | OHADA 309 permits a one-or-more-member SARL with liability limited to contributions; 385 permits an SA with a single shareholder; 853-1 permits one-or-more-member SAS with articles setting governance subject to mandatory rules. A branch lacks separate legal personality under 117. Choose governance, liability and regulated-activity requirements before comparing tax. | [OHADA309,385,853-1,117](https://acpce.cg/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/ACTE-UNIFORME-REVISE-RELATIF-AU-DROIT-DES-SOCIETES-COMMERCIALES-ET-DU-GROUPEMENT-DINTERET-ECONOMIQUE.pdf); ledger F01 |

rows.text: | SARL form of articles | Congo decree 2 permits private or notarised SARL articles; deposit of privately signed articles in notarial minutes is not compulsory. 3 lists required company, capital, shareholder, contribution and governance particulars. The simplification is not a blanket exemption from preparing valid articles or capital evidence. | [Decree2017-41 arts2–3](https://acpce.cg/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/congo-decret_2017-41_sarl.pdf); ledger F05 |

rows.text: | Registered office | OHADA 25 requires a sufficiently precise address/geographic location, not only a post-office box. ACPCE accepts ownership, lease, utility/internet or other office evidence under its public checklist; do not invent a mandatory separate commercial-office lease. | [OHADA25;ACPCE creation checklist](https://acpce.cg/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/ACTE-UNIFORME-REVISE-RELATIF-AU-DROIT-DES-SOCIETES-COMMERCIALES-ET-DU-GROUPEMENT-DINTERET-ECONOMIQUE.pdf); ledger F06 |

rows.text: | SARL audit thresholds | OHADA 376 requires at least 1 statutory auditor if 2of3conditions at year-end hold: balance sheet over XAF 125,000,000, annual turnover over XAF 250,000,000, permanent employees over 50. Falling outside 2criteria for the 2 years before mandate expiry releases the obligation; a qualifying minority can seek appointment in court even below thresholds. | [OHADA376](https://acpce.cg/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/ACTE-UNIFORME-REVISE-RELATIF-AU-DROIT-DES-SOCIETES-COMMERCIALES-ET-DU-GROUPEMENT-DINTERET-ECONOMIQUE.pdf); ledger F13 |

Keep governance, accounting, tax and beneficial-ownership filings as separate checklists; complete current filing obligations are not all verified here. | [OHADA694;CGI130–131](https://acpce.cg/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/ACTE-UNIFORME-REVISE-RELATIF-AU-DROIT-DES-SOCIETES-COMMERCIALES-ET-DU-GROUPEMENT-DINTERET-ECONOMIQUE.pdf); ledger F14 |

rows.text: Follow F09's advertised official route: establish the applicant account, complete the unique form and upload the applicable checklist documents, confirm official assessed fees, pay through the official flow, then retain delivered electronic documents and acknowledgements. rows.text: | Official identity checklist | ACPCE requires valid identity for director, members/shareholders and SA auditor; legal-person shareholder RCCM where applicable; foreign resident/long-stay documentation and criminal-record/honour declaration as listed; director's personal NIU and photo, marriage record where applicable. Do not collect irrelevant items without checking the actual applicant category. | [ACPCE create a company, identity section](https://acpce.cg/creer-une-societe/); ledger F07 |

rows.text: | Constitutional checklist | ACPCE lists SARL/SARLU private/notarised articles plus regularity/conformity declaration; other forms' notarised articles and notarised subscription/payment statement; SA constitutive-meeting minutes and capital-deposit proof. rows.text: | Foreign branch conversion | OHADA 116–120 requires branch RCCM registration; a foreign owner's branch must be contributed to an existing/new company of an OHADA State within 2 years unless the competent commerce minister grants dispensation. Subject to special-regime companies, dispensation lasts 2 years non-renewable. Do not promise conversion only into a Congo subsidiary. | [OHADA116–120](https://acpce.cg/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/ACTE-UNIFORME-REVISE-RELATIF-AU-DROIT-DES-SOCIETES-COMMERCIALES-ET-DU-GROUPEMENT-DINTERET-ECONOMIQUE.pdf); ledger F11 |

rows.text: **Draft scope:** Companies within IS under CGI 2; special petroleum, integration and investment approvals are outside the completed computation. This is Republic of Congo(CG), not DR Congo(CD). Independent pack review is pending. Initial 2026 law is not represented as a fully consolidated or operational 2026 position.

rows.text: | General and sector rates | Initial 2026 law: general IS 28%; microfinance and private education organised as a company 25%; mines/quarries and property operations 28%; foreign legal persons 33%. Hydrocarbon exploration, production, storage and transport use their contract rate, no lower than ordinary law. Round taxable profit down to the lower XAF 1,000. | [CGI86A](https://sgg.cg/JO/2026/congo-jo-2026-3-3.pdf); ledger C01 |
rows.review: Read in full Guide review; case values and legal conditions checked separately in cases.json; legal limbs traced in rule-coverage.json. F01/F02/F03/F04 findings take precedence.

rows.text: | Minimum tax | Minimum perception is 1% of total operating, financial and non-ordinary receipts, excluding receipts already subject to final withholding. Compare this minimum with ordinary IS; do not use only sales turnover or reinstate the old unsupported fixed minimum floors. | [CGI86C(1)–(3)](https://sgg.cg/JO/2026/congo-jo-2026-3-3.pdf); ledger C08 |
rows.review: Read in full Guide review; case values and legal conditions checked separately in cases.json; legal limbs traced in rule-coverage.json. F01/F02/F03/F04 findings take precedence.

rows.text: Prepare an accounting-to-tax reconciliation. Test each cost against C04, remove IS and penalties, apply the interest limits and eligible losses, then round the taxable profit as C01 requires. Compare ordinary IS against C08 and credit only substantiated same-year payments. The examples assume no foreign credits, incentives or separate solidarity levy. The old blanket 5% surtax is not confirmed and is excluded.
rows.review: Read in full Guide review; case values and legal conditions checked separately in cases.json; legal limbs traced in rule-coverage.json. F01/F02/F03/F04 findings take precedence.

rows.text: | Taxable entities | Companies including single-member SA, SAS and SARL are within IS by form; public entities and other bodies conducting taxable commercial activities are within its activity scope. Partnership options and statutory exemptions must be considered separately. | [CGI2–3](https://sgg.cg/JO/2026/congo-jo-2026-3-3.pdf); ledger C02 |
rows.review: Read in full Guide review; case values and legal conditions checked separately in cases.json; legal limbs traced in rule-coverage.json. F01/F02/F03/F04 findings take precedence.

rows.text: | Tax base and accounts | Determine taxable net profit from all taxable receipts less allowable costs using OHADA accounting or applicable regulated-sector rules. Accounts ordinarily close 31December; tax is assessed on the preceding financial year. | [CGI6,9](https://sgg.cg/JO/2026/congo-jo-2026-3-3.pdf); ledger C03 |
rows.review: Read in full Guide review; case values and legal conditions checked separately in cases.json; legal limbs traced in rule-coverage.json. F01/F02/F03/F04 findings take precedence.

rows.text: | Conditions for deductions | Costs must belong to the year, serve the business, be real and supported, reduce net assets, and not support exempt receipts or be legally excluded/abnormal management. Domestic supplier invoices require the NIU and SFEC. Cash payments of XAF 200,000 or more fail the deduction condition. Do not import VAT's strictly-greater-than boundary into IS. | [CGI25](https://sgg.cg/JO/2026/congo-jo-2026-3-3.pdf); ledger C04 |
rows.review: Read in full Guide review; case values and legal conditions checked separately in cases.json; legal limbs traced in rule-coverage.json. F01/F02/F03/F04 findings take precedence.

rows.text: | Tax and penalties | IS itself is not deductible; taxes borne by the enterprise and assessed during the year can be deductible. Fines, confiscations and penalties are excluded. Later refunds of deductible taxes enter receipts. | [CGI42](https://sgg.cg/JO/2026/congo-jo-2026-3-3.pdf); ledger C05 |
rows.review: Read in full Guide review; case values and legal conditions checked separately in cases.json; legal limbs traced in rule-coverage.json. F01/F02/F03/F04 findings take precedence.

rows.text: | Interest restriction | Interest must meet the ordinary conditions and market pricing. Related-shareholder/group interest additionally requires fully paid capital and is limited by BEAC tender rate plus 3 points. Total annual net interest is capped at 20% of OHADA gross operating surplus attributable to non-exempt activity, with disallowed interest carryforward up to 5 years subject to the same conditions. The cap excludes qualifying finance/insurance operating-charge interest. No live BEAC rate is supplied. | [CGI49](https://sgg.cg/JO/2026/congo-jo-2026-3-3.pdf); ledger C06 |
rows.review: Read in full Guide review; case values and legal conditions checked separately in cases.json; legal limbs traced in rule-coverage.json. F01/F02/F03/F04 findings take precedence.

rows.text: | Losses | Ordinary losses carry forward through the fifth year after the loss year. Depreciation booked during losses is treated as ordinary losses. Losses from IS-exempt years cannot carry forward. | [CGI75](https://sgg.cg/JO/2026/congo-jo-2026-3-3.pdf); ledger C07 |
rows.review: Read in full Guide review; case values and legal conditions checked separately in cases.json; legal limbs traced in rule-coverage.json. F01/F02/F03/F04 findings take precedence.

rows.text: Identify the competent fiscal residence, retain the NIU, existence filing, DSF schedules, payment references and electronic acknowledgements. C10 records the unresolved filing-date conflict. Do not infer that a public calendar verifies the live portal fields or successful filing.

rows.text: | Minimum declaration and instalments | Declare the current-year minimum by 15March using preceding-year/last-closed-year receipts provisionally. Pay four minimum-tax instalments by 15March,15June,15September and 15December. The minimum credits against same-year IS, but remains with Treasury where ordinary liability is lower or nil. | [CGI86C(4)–(7)](https://sgg.cg/JO/2026/congo-jo-2026-3-3.pdf); ledger C09 |

rows.text: | Annual statutory rule | CGI 86F requires the profit/loss return within 4 months of year-end; 86G requires the balance on delivery. The official 2026 ACPCE calendar instead states 15May for IS/DSF. These are conflicting sources: retain the statutory wording here, flag the administrative date, and stop short of an operative 2026 filing instruction until reconciled. | [CGI86F–G; compare ACPCE2026calendar](https://sgg.cg/JO/2026/congo-jo-2026-3-3.pdf); ledger C10 |
rows.review: Read in full Guide review; case values and legal conditions checked separately in cases.json; legal limbs traced in rule-coverage.json. F01/F02/F03/F04 findings take precedence.

rows.text: | Existence and filing package | Submit the existence declaration within 15 days of beginning operations. The annual DSF follows the prescribed model, with financial statements, tax reconciliation and identification schedules. CGI 131 specifies 3 complete sets plus electronic statements. CGI 130 requires real-regime electronic declaration/payment and appropriate accountant certification where no statutory auditor exists. rows.text: **Draft scope:** Congo enterprises, foreign companies, branches, service suppliers and investors. This Guide does not certify a treaty network, current tax-residence certificate process or complete departure clearance. Independent pack review is pending. rows.text: | Project and service PE tests | 4A lists fixed places and deems a construction/assembly/installation/supervision project a PE when lasting more than 3 months. Services through personnel for the same/connected project create a PE when exceeding 183 days in any 12 months. Equality alone does not satisfy these specific duration limbs, but a fixed place or agency can independently create a PE. | [CGI4A(1)–(2)](https://sgg.cg/JO/2026/congo-jo-2026-3-3.pdf); ledger X02 |
rows.review: Read in full Guide review; case values and legal conditions checked separately in cases.json; legal limbs traced in rule-coverage.json. F01/F02/F03/F04 findings take precedence.

rows.text: | Nonresident services/royalties | Subject to applicable treaties,86D imposes 20% IS withholding on payments by a resident company or for a nonresident company's PE for services rendered by nonresidents or royalties paid to them. Royalties include rights, equipment, know-how and software acquisition/rental as stated. Classify actual contracts first; do not apply the old miscellaneous reduced-rate list by default. | [CGI86D](https://sgg.cg/JO/2026/congo-jo-2026-3-3.pdf); ledger X05 |
rows.review: Read in full Guide review; case values and legal conditions checked separately in cases.json; legal limbs traced in rule-coverage.json. F01/F02/F03/F04 findings take precedence.

rows.text: Identify the legal person, effective management and actual operations. Test X01–X04 before selecting an ordinary PE or special intermittent regime. Classify each payment by nature and recipient, locate performance and source, then test any actually applicable treaty. Keep contracts, duration logs, personnel schedules, beneficial-ownership evidence and foreign tax documents.

rows.text: | Corporate territory | Enterprises registered in Congo or effectively managed there are resident enterprises; non-residents with a Congo PE are operated in Congo. Nonresident PE profit attribution includes the PE, same/similar goods sales and same/similar industrial/commercial activities in Congo under 7. Do not assume worldwide exemption or only invoiced branch profits. | [CGI4,7](https://sgg.cg/JO/2026/congo-jo-2026-3-3.pdf); ledger X01 |

rows.text: | Preparatory exceptions and fragmentation | Storage/exhibition, processing by another enterprise, purchasing/information and other listed activities need the relevant preparatory/auxiliary limitation. Anti-fragmentation denies the exception for linked complementary business functions, an existing PE or a combined non-auxiliary activity. Do not split one coherent business across sites to claim a warehouse exemption. | [CGI4A(3)–(4)](https://sgg.cg/JO/2026/congo-jo-2026-3-3.pdf); ledger X03 |

rows.text: | Agency, insurance and control | Habitual contract conclusion/principal negotiating role or habitual stock delivery can create an agency PE. Nonresident insurers have the stated premium/risk rule except reinsurance. An ordinary independent agent can fall outside these limbs; near-exclusive activity for closely linked enterprises prevents independence. Control alone does not create a PE. 4A(8)–(9) define close links, including more-than 50% tests, but other actual control is relevant. | [CGI4A(5)–(9)](https://sgg.cg/JO/2026/congo-jo-2026-3-3.pdf); ledger X04 |

rows.text: | Foreign receipts and double tax | 11 brings foreign PE results belonging to a CEMAC company and foreign dividends, interest, royalties and service fees of an enterprise operated in Congo into the stated tax base. Double tax can be relieved by foreign-tax deduction or a credit limited to Congo tax on the same income, subject to actual entitlement. Foreign PE losses are restricted to later PE profits within 5 years. Do not use both relief routes for the same amount. | [CGI11](https://sgg.cg/JO/2026/congo-jo-2026-3-3.pdf); ledger X06 |

rows.text: | Special intermittent foreign enterprise | 92 concerns foreign legal entities whose intermittent/precarious activities do not permit the ordinary 86C–F regime. 92A fixes 22% of qualifying tax-exclusive Congo turnover as deemed profit and 92C points to 86A, whose foreign-person rate is 33%. Thus 7.26% is the derived IS alone, not a universal service withholding rate or all-in burden. Mobilisation, reimbursed supplies and chain subcontract exclusions have cumulative conditions not certified in this short computation. | [CGI92–92C](https://sgg.cg/JO/2026/congo-jo-2026-3-3.pdf); ledger X07 |

Use the income Guide for the IRCM base/rate; 106 fusion relief has its own conditions. | [CGI107](https://sgg.cg/JO/2026/congo-jo-2026-3-3.pdf); ledger X10 |

Foreign branch directors have a residence presumption; treaties and government-posting provisions affect the answer. This is not a universal 183-day test. | [CGI93B](https://sgg.cg/JO/2026/congo-jo-2026-3-3.pdf); ledger I05 |

rows.text: | Salary benefits and deductible pension amount | Start with gross cash and benefits. Benefits use actual value, or statutory defaults: housing 20% of salary capped for social security; domestic staff/security 7%, utilities 5%, telephone 2%, car 3%, food 20% of gross. The reference base deducts specified pension/mandatory-social amounts. Employer mutual premiums are not taxable if benefiting all employees. ITS then allows 20% deduction after the employee retirement contribution. Social contribution rates/ceilings are not established here. | [CGI115–116](https://sgg.cg/JO/2026/congo-jo-2026-3-3.pdf); ledger I14 |

rows.text: | Family quotient | Round net taxable salary down to XAF 1,000 before dividing by parts; tax the quotient and multiply by parts. Basic parts: single/divorced/widowed without dependants 1; married without dependants 2; single/divorced with 1child2; married/widowed with 1child2.5; each additional child adds 0.5, maximum 6.5. Separate-employed spouses are each treated as married, children assigned to husband absent express exception. A childless widow(er) is treated as married for 2 years following death. Special 116C situations remain a referral. | [CGI116A–116C](https://sgg.cg/JO/2026/congo-jo-2026-3-3.pdf); ledger I15 |

Use 1January family facts except marriage/increased dependants during the year uses 31December or death date. rows.text: | Arm's-length adjustment | For enterprises dependent on/controlling foreign enterprises, including common foreign control, profits indirectly shifted through purchase/sale prices or other means are restored to Congo results. Lack of documents permits assessment from available information; comparable enterprises and functional/comparability/industry analyses are relevant. rows.text: | Ordinary VAT and additional centimes | The ministry-hosted VAT law 17 states ordinary 18%; the 2026 state-invoice rule 7.2.4(d) repeats 18% of the pretax price and centimes at 5% of VAT. VAT 36B says centimes are non-deductible. Thus an ordinary 18%-rated transaction has VAT 18% plus centimes 0.9% of base, not 23% of base. The complete later amendment chain is not closed. | [VAT17,36B; FinanceAct2026,7.2.4(d)](https://sgg.cg/JO/2026/congo-jo-2026-3-3.pdf); ledger V01 |

rows.text: | Other rates require classification | The ACPCE 2026 calendar lists 5% reduced and 0% VAT alongside 18%. The 2026 Finance Act replaces Annex 3(exempt essential goods) and Annex 5(reduced-rate ordinary-consumption goods). A listed tariff code and actual product must be matched before selecting relief; old forestry/SEZ and export eligibility are not fully verified here. | [ACPCE2026calendar p2; FinanceAct2026 VATannexes3,5](https://acpce.cg/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Calendrier-des-obligations-fiscales-et-sociales-au-titre-de-lannee-2026.pdf); ledger V02 |

rows.text: Classify the supply and tax point before choosing a rate. V01 establishes the ordinary VAT/centimes arithmetic; V02 requires actual tariff/relief evidence. Separate deductible VAT from non-deductible centimes. Apply V05 and all other input restrictions; do not claim that merely staying under the cash boundary proves input eligibility.

rows.text: | Economic operations and base | The ministry compilation's VAT 1–5 includes remunerated independent economic supplies of goods/services, imports and specified self-supplies. 12 uses consideration for goods/services and nearest-XAF 1,000 base rounding; 13 includes customs value plus duty/excise for imports. The compilation is a historical baseline, not a 2026 consolidation. | [VAT1–5,12–13 in ministry compilation](https://www.finances.gouv.cg/sites/default/files/documents/CGI%20Tome%20I.pdf); ledger V03 |

rows.text: | Tax event versus exigibility | In the historical compilation 10–11, delivery is the goods event and service performance is the service event; goods tax is generally exigible at delivery and services/works at receipts including advances, with a permitted debits basis. Imports are exigible at customs consumption declaration. Do not confuse invoice issue with every liability date; later changes remain to reconcile. | [VAT10–11 in ministry compilation](https://www.finances.gouv.cg/sites/default/files/documents/CGI%20Tome%20I.pdf); ledger V04 |

rows.text: | 2026 cash input restriction | The 2026 amendment to VAT 24 excludes input tax on cash-paid expenses whose amount EXCEEDS XAF 200,000. At exactly 200,000 this particular exclusion is not triggered; other input conditions still apply. The IS deduction boundary in CGI 25 is different and excludes cash at equality. | [VAT24(1)(7) as amended2026](https://sgg.cg/JO/2026/congo-jo-2026-3-3.pdf); ledger V05 |
